transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. Here are the specifics. District learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed this maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice has not yet been attached to the remote-day draft. This means the draft plan's assumption that instruction can begin through the LMS at 8:00 a.m. is not viable. My recommendation is that instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m. This approach does not rely on LMS authentication, so students and teachers can access materials even while the system is down. This also complements Tasha's printed packet plan for the 38 households without reliable internet, since the PDFs can be printed for those families. I'd note that this IT adjustment needs to be reflected in the revised plan before you sign off, Dr. Lee.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Daniel. From a transportation perspective, I want to confirm that the on-site meal pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is feasible and ready to implement — my team can coordinate staffing for those pickup sites. Regarding Tasha's printed packet distribution, I agree that combining packet pickup at the same meal pickup sites is the most efficient approach given that no buses can safely run. For families who cannot travel to those sites, volunteer or staff drivers would be the backup option, though I'd want to confirm we have enough volunteers with vehicles safe for tomorrow's road conditions. Dr. Lee, from my side, the transportation-related elements of the revised plan would be: meals available for on-site pickup at North and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., no bus-based delivery or routes operating, and coordination with Tasha's team on packet pickup at those same sites. I'm ready for your decision once all elements are confirmed.
